The rules that apply in Maharashtra

  • Maharashtra Fire Prevention and Life Safety Measures Act, 2006. Owners and occupiers must install the required fire prevention and life safety measures and keep them in good working order. Twice a year, in January and July, they must give the Chief Fire Officer a certificate in Form B, issued by a licensed agency, confirming the systems are maintained.
  • National Building Code of India 2016, Part 4 (Fire and Life Safety). Sets the requirements for exits, detection, firefighting systems and compartmentation, depending on the building's use and height.
  • Fire NOC. Buildings need fire department approval at the planning stage and before occupation. Tenants should check whether their fit-out changes sprinklers, detectors, exits or fire compartments, because those changes may need approval too.

Choosing the right fire extinguisher

TypeBest forAvoid on
ABC dry powderGeneral office areas: paper, wood, fabric, flammable liquids and gasesServer rooms and sensitive electronics, because the powder leaves a corrosive residue
Carbon dioxide (CO2)Electrical panels, UPS rooms, server roomsLarge open areas, where the gas disperses quickly
Clean agentServer rooms, data centres, control roomsNot a substitute for a fixed suppression system in large server halls
FoamFlammable liquids, such as fuel stores and generator roomsLive electrical equipment
Wet chemical (Class K)Commercial kitchens with cooking oil and fat firesElectrical fires

Selection, installation and maintenance of portable extinguishers in India follow Indian Standard IS 2190.

Fixed systems

  • Fire alarm and detection: smoke and heat detectors, manual call points and hooters, with addressable systems that show exactly which detector triggered.
  • Sprinklers that discharge water automatically over a fire.
  • Hydrants and hose reels fed by fire pumps and a dedicated water tank.
  • Gas suppression for server rooms, UPS rooms and data centres, where water would cause damage.
  • Emergency lighting and exit signage that keep escape routes visible during a power failure.
  • Public address and voice evacuation systems for larger buildings.

Maintenance that keeps you compliant

Installed equipment only protects you, and only satisfies the law, if it works. A maintenance programme covers regular visual checks of extinguishers, periodic servicing, refilling and pressure testing, testing of alarm panels and detectors, running fire pumps on schedule, checking emergency lighting, and recording all of it. Mock evacuation drills and staff training complete the picture. We keep the records ready for your Form B certificate and for inspections.

What a fire safety audit covers

  • Escape routes: exits, staircases, doors, signage and travel distances
  • Fire compartmentation and openings in fire-rated walls
  • Housekeeping and storage, especially in stores, basements and electrical rooms
  • Electrical hazards: overloaded sockets, open panels and poor cable management
  • Condition and coverage of detection, alarm and firefighting systems
  • Staff training, fire wardens and evacuation drill records
  • Documentation: NOCs, Form B certificates, service records and test reports

You receive a report of findings ranked by risk, with a clear action plan.

FAQs

Fire Safety Equipment & Compliance: common questions

How often must the Form B certificate be submitted in Maharashtra?

Twice a year, in January and July. It must be issued by a licensed agency and confirms that the building's fire prevention and life safety systems are maintained.

Which fire extinguisher should we use in a server room?

Carbon dioxide or clean agent extinguishers. Dry powder works on electrical fires but leaves a residue that can damage electronics. Larger server rooms and data centres should also have a fixed gas suppression system.

Does our office fit-out need fire department approval?

If the fit-out changes sprinklers, detectors, exits or fire compartments, it may. Check with your building management and the fire authority before work starts. We can assess this during design.

Can you take over maintenance of systems installed by another vendor?

Yes. We start with an inspection of the existing systems and records, list anything that needs fixing, and then maintain the systems under an AMC.
